{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My mother-in-law had criticized everything about me for a decade—my career, my parenting, my cooking. When I was hospitalized unexpectedly, she moved into our house for six weeks, handled everything perfectly, and never once complained. She held my hand through physical therapy. I never knew she had that in her.

CANDIDATE A:
My mother-in-law had criticized everything about me for a decade. When I was hospitalized unexpectedly, she visited once, commented that the flowers my husband brought were 'a bit much,' and suggested I was probably exaggerating how sick I felt. The crisis revealed nothing new—she was exactly who she'd always been.

CANDIDATE B:
The class clown who disrupted every lesson and seemed to care about nothing witnessed a student collapse during an assembly. While teachers froze, he performed CPR he'd learned from a YouTube video, kept her alive until paramedics arrived, then went back to making jokes the next day. The mask hid a different person.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:37"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories reveal an unexpected positive side of a person previously perceived negatively, showing hidden depth and capability during a crisis."}
